units.title: Hedging: cautious, precise claims
units.summary: Sound academic and balanced instead of absolute.

cards.title: Why hedge?
cards.body: Academic writers avoid claims that are too strong to defend. Compare: *Video games cause violence.* (easy to disprove) with *Some research suggests that violent games may increase aggression in some children.* (careful and credible)

cards.title: Hedging tools
rows: tend to, seem to, appear to, suggest, indicate
generally, often, usually, largely, arguably, possibly
some, many, most, a number of
to some extent, in many cases, it is likely that

items: Everyone agrees that technology is bad.
Many people believe that technology has some negative effects.
Social media can damage some relationships.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Band 7+ Task Response rewards **well-supported, balanced** positions. Hedging also adds grammatical range.
examples: Stricter laws are likely to reduce crime to some extent, although they are unlikely to solve the problem entirely.

practice.q: Which sentence is best hedged?
o: Excessive homework may be counter-productive for younger children.
practice.a: Excessive homework may be counter-productive for younger children.

practice.q: Young people ___ spend more time online than older adults.
practice.a: tend to

practice.q: This policy ___ reduce unemployment, but the evidence is limited.
practice.a: could

practice.q: All teenagers [are] addicted to their phones.
It is ___ (like) that prices will continue to rise.
Put the words in order.
practice.a: This approach is likely to be effective in many cases.

units.title: Linking words: accurate and varied
units.summary: However, therefore, moreover — meaning, position and punctuation.

cards.title: Linkers by function
rows: however, nevertheless, on the other hand, in contrast
therefore, as a result, consequently, thus
for example, for instance, such as, in particular
in conclusion, overall, to sum up

cards.title: Position and punctuation
cards.body: Sentence linkers usually start a sentence and are followed by a comma: *However, …* They can also go after the subject: *This, however, is not the whole story.* **such as** introduces a list inside a sentence, not a new sentence.
examples: Cars are convenient. However, they are expensive to run.
Many sports, such as football and cricket, are played in teams.

cards.title: Don't overuse
cards.body: Band 6 uses linkers 'mechanically'. Band 7 uses them **flexibly** — and also links ideas with reference (*this problem*, *such policies*).

items: On the other hand, I think it is good. (no first hand)
However, I think it is good.
'On the other hand' contrasts with a previous side.
For example, cars, buses and trains.
For example, cars and buses cause pollution.
A full sentence is needed after 'For example,'.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Choosing the **right** linker (not just any linker) is part of Coherence and Cohesion.
examples: Public transport is cheaper than driving. As a result, many commuters have switched to trains.

practice.q: Tourism creates jobs. ___, it can damage the environment.
practice.a: However

practice.q: Prices fell sharply. ___, sales doubled.
practice.a: As a result

practice.q: Exercise improves mood. ___, it reduces the risk of disease.
practice.a: Furthermore

practice.q: Many fruits, [for example] mangoes and bananas, are grown here.
Which is punctuated correctly?
o: The plan is cheap, however it is slow.
The plan is cheap. However, it is slow.
The plan is cheap however, it is slow.
practice.a: The plan is cheap. However, it is slow.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: This approach, however, has several disadvantages.

units.title: Expressing cause and effect
units.summary: lead to, result in, be caused by, contribute to, stem from.

cards.title: Cause → effect
rows: Poor diet can lead to heart disease.
The policy resulted in lower emissions.
Urbanisation has given rise to new problems.

cards.title: Effect ← cause
rows: Floods are often caused by deforestation.
The problem stems from poor planning.
The delay was due to bad weather.
The fall can be attributed to higher prices.

items: This leads to people buy more.
This leads to people buying more. / This leads people to buy more.
Obesity is resulted from poor diet.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Problem–solution and cause essays need several ways to express causation; repeating 'cause' limits Lexical and Grammatical range.
examples: The decline in rural employment has contributed to rapid urban growth.

practice.q: Lack of sleep can ___ poor concentration.
practice.a: lead to

practice.q: Many health problems ___ an unhealthy diet.
practice.a: result from

practice.q: Traffic congestion is [resulted from] the growing number of cars.
The increase can be attributed ___ lower interest rates.
Which is correct?
o: Advertising leads to children want junk food.
Advertising leads children to want junk food.
Advertising leads to children wanting junk food.
practice.a: Advertising leads children to want junk food.
practice.x: lead + object + to-infinitive (or lead to + noun/-ing).

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: The problem stems from a lack of investment.

units.title: Giving opinions and generalising
units.summary: Clear positions without 'I think' in every sentence.

cards.title: Stating your view
rows: In my view, … · I would argue that … · I firmly believe that …
It seems clear that … · There is little doubt that …
I agree to some extent that … · While I accept that …, I believe …

cards.title: Talking about others
rows: It is often argued that … · Some people claim that …
In general, … · On the whole, … · Most people …
This is not always the case, however.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Task 2 needs a **clear position throughout** (band 7). State it in the introduction and conclusion.
examples: While technology has made life more convenient, I would argue that its effect on family life has been largely negative.

practice.q: [According to me], the government should act.
I [am agree] that homework is useful.
___ argued that zoos protect endangered species.
practice.a: It is often

practice.q: Which shows a partly agree position?
o: I agree to some extent, but…
practice.a: I agree to some extent, but…

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: I would argue that education should be free.

units.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences
units.summary: It is … that … and What … is … to focus the reader's attention.

cards.title: It-cleft
cards.body: **It is / was + focus + that / who + rest**
examples: It is the cost of housing that worries young people most.
It was only in 2010 that the law changed.

cards.title: What-cleft
examples: What cities need is better public transport.
What surprised me was how friendly people were.

items: What we need it is more teachers.
What we need is more teachers.
It is the cost what matters.
It is the cost that matters.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Cleft sentences add emphasis and are a clear sign of grammatical range in Speaking.
examples: What I really enjoy about my hometown is the sense of community.

practice.q: ___ young people need is good career advice.
practice.a: What

practice.q: It is the government ___ should take responsibility.
practice.a: that

practice.q: What I like most [it] is the food.
Put the words in order.
practice.a: What cities need is better public transport.

units.title: Inversion for emphasis
units.summary: Not only…but also, rarely, never, only when — used sparingly.

cards.title: Negative adverbials first
cards.body: After **not only, never, rarely, seldom, hardly, only when, not until, under no circumstances** at the start, use **question word order**.
examples: Not only does exercise improve health, but it also reduces stress.
Rarely have so many people moved to cities in such a short time.
Only when prices fall will people buy more.

items: Not only does exercise improve health…

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: One accurate inversion shows C1 range; several in a row sound unnatural.
examples: Not only would free transport reduce traffic, but it would also cut emissions.

practice.q: Which is correct?
o: Not only it is cheap, but also fast.
Not only is it cheap, but it is also fast.
Not only it cheap is, but also fast.
practice.a: Not only is it cheap, but it is also fast.

practice.q: Rarely [people have] seen such growth.
Only when the rain stopped ___ the match continue.
practice.a: did

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: Never have so many people used social media.
